title: POST
definition: An HTTP method used to send data to a server to CREATE a new resource.
simpleExplanation: If GET is reading a book, POST is writing a completely new book. The client bundles up a package of data (like a filled-out signup form) and hands it to the server. The server takes that data and creates something new in its database.
realWorldExample: Creating a new Twitter account. Submitting a new comment on a YouTube video. Uploading a photo to Instagram.

basic: Where is the data placed in a POST request?

answers.question: Where is data placed?
answers.answer: In the HTTP Request Body. Unlike GET requests, POST data is hidden inside the body payload, not exposed in the URL.

answers.question: Is it Idempotent?
answers.answer: NO! Calling POST 1 time creates 1 user. Calling POST 10 times creates 10 duplicate users. It is not idempotent because the server state changes every single time.
